7 Brew German Chocolate Mocha: Price, Calories & Recipe

A medium German Chocolate Mocha is about $4.95, with 370 calories, 120 mg of caffeine and 56 g of sugar. Every number here comes from 7 Brew's own published nutrition guide, broken out by size and preparation.

Is there a sugar-free German Chocolate Mocha?

Yes — 7 Brew lists a sugar-free version built with sugar-free syrups. Comparing mediums (iced):

VersionCaloriesSugarCarbsCaffeine
German Chocolate Mocha37056 g59 g120 mg
Sugar-free German Chocolate Mocha3806 g23 g120 mg

Caffeine does not change — only the syrup does. See every sugar-free option in the customization guide.

Compare this swap with all 44 sugar-free drinks on the sugar-free menu page.

German Chocolate Mocha allergens

7 Brew's published allergen guide lists Milk for the German Chocolate Mocha. Adding a milk, syrup or topping changes this, and every drink is made on shared equipment, so cross-contact is possible.

If you are ordering around an allergy, check the full allergen and dietary guide and confirm at the window.

How to order a German Chocolate Mocha

Ask for it by name — it is on the standard board at every 7 Brew, so no special script is needed. Say the size first, then the drink: "Can I get a medium German Chocolate Mocha?"

Worth knowing before you order: the base is customisable. You can swap milk, ask for sugar-free syrups, change the sweetness level, or have most drinks made iced, hot or blended as a frozen chiller where the menu allows. Ordering through the app earns 100 rewards points either way.

Make a German Chocolate at Home (Copycat Recipe)

This is the drink people think got discontinued, so the recipe requests never stop. The home version follows the stand's formula: chocolate, coconut and caramel in equal balance, espresso, and milk. Like the cake it is named after, the coconut and caramel are what make it German chocolate rather than a plain mocha.

For one medium iced German Chocolate (24 oz cup)

  • 2 shots of espresso (about 2 oz), hot
  • 1 oz chocolate sauce
  • 1/2 oz coconut syrup
  • 1/2 oz caramel sauce
  • About 8 oz milk
  • A full cup of ice
  1. Pour the chocolate sauce, coconut syrup and caramel sauce into the cup.
  2. Add the hot espresso and stir. The heat melts everything together.
  3. Fill the cup with ice, then pour the milk over the top.
  4. Stir once and drink.

Hot version: steam the milk, skip the ice, same sauces and shots. Sugar-free version: swap in sugar-free chocolate, coconut and caramel syrups. At the stand, the sugar-free medium runs 380 calories with 6 g of sugar, going by the official guide. Chiller version: blend everything with the ice until smooth. The stand's large chiller reaches 930 calories, so treat the blended one as dessert.

Is the German Chocolate Still at 7 Brew?

Yes. Search results keep asking because the drink moved around the menu board, and some fans report it filed under Classics now instead of Originals. The hard evidence: it carries full rows in 7 Brew's current official nutrition guide (October 2026), which only lists live drinks, in iced, hot, frozen chiller and sugar-free versions. If your stand's board does not show it, order a German Chocolate Mocha by name, or ask for a mocha with coconut and caramel.

7 Brew German Chocolate Mocha FAQ

How many calories are in a 7 Brew German Chocolate Mocha?

A medium iced German Chocolate Mocha has 370 calories. A small has 260 and a large 430, according to 7 Brew's nutrition guide.

How much caffeine is in a 7 Brew German Chocolate Mocha?

About 120 mg in a medium. Small is 120 mg and large is 240 mg.

How much does a 7 Brew German Chocolate Mocha cost?

Roughly $4.25 for a small, $4.95 for a medium and $5.75 for a large. Prices are our estimates and vary by stand — every 7 Brew is independently owned.

How much sugar is in a 7 Brew German Chocolate Mocha?

56 g in a medium, or 6 g if you order the sugar-free version.

What is in a 7 Brew German Chocolate?

Chocolate, coconut and caramel, the German chocolate cake trio, in a mocha: espresso and milk with chocolate sauce, coconut syrup and caramel syrup. It is a milk mocha, not a half-and-half breve, which is why a medium iced is 370 calories instead of the 500-plus of the Original breves.

Is the German Chocolate still at 7 Brew?

Yes. It has full rows in 7 Brew's current official nutrition guide (October 2026), which only lists live menu drinks. Some stands now file it with the Classics rather than the Originals, and fans sometimes cannot spot it on the board. Order it by name, German Chocolate Mocha, or describe it as a mocha with coconut and caramel.

How many calories are in a German Chocolate chiller?

The frozen chiller is the heavy version: 460 calories in a small, 660 in a medium and 930 in a large. That large ties the White Chocolate Mocha chiller as the highest-calorie drink on the 7 Brew menu.

How many calories are in the sugar-free German Chocolate?

A sugar-free medium iced has 380 calories and 6 g of sugar. That is higher than the regular medium iced at 370 calories, per the official guide. Sugar-free swaps the syrups and drops the sugar from 56 g to 6 g, but it does not make this the lighter drink.

How do I make a 7 Brew German Chocolate at home?

For a medium iced: 1 oz chocolate sauce, 1/2 oz coconut syrup and 1/2 oz caramel sauce, 2 shots of espresso, and about 8 oz of milk over ice. The full copycat recipe is in the recipe section on this page.
